the SAR for these tricyclic compounds is similar to that for the bicyclic pyridyl N-methyl amide analogues, and that the 3-bromopyridyl N-oxides are a new class of FPT inhibitors.

the SAR of the 3-substituent of these tricyclic FPT inhibitors can be summarized by the following generalizations: (1) the 3-position is a critical site for activity and (2) the 3-halogenated analogues are potent and active.
3-substituents on the tricycic pyridine ring are tolerated, but bulky groups are not.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the pyridinylacetic acid moiety of these compounds is the most important for FPT inhibition and that the tricyclocycloheptapyridine ring system is a very good scaffold for the synthesis of potent and orally bioavailable FPT inhibitors.

a small alkyl group at the 3 position of the tricylic pyridine system is optimal for potency, whereas a bulky alkyl group such as a tert-butyl group or a polar group such as a hydroxyl or amine is not tolerated.
the 3-bromopyridine N-oxide amides are a new class of potent FPT inhibitors that have in vivo antitumorigenic activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 3-substituents on the pyridine ring of tricyclic FPT inhibitors have a profound influence on their in vitro potency and in vivo antitumorigenic activity.
the 3-bromopyridyl N-oxides 38 and 40 are potent and selective FPT inhibitors with good oral bioavailability.
the 3-bromine atom is a crucial structural element in this class of compounds.
